object.title: Sturmfels–Sullivant conjecture on normality and Cohen–Macaulayness of cut ideals
object.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. For each unordered partition $A|B$ of $V(G)$, let $q_{A|B}$ be a variable, and let $I_G$ be the kernel of the cut map defining the cut variety of $G$; thus $K[q]/I_G$ is its semigroup algebra. **Sturmfels–Sullivant conjecture.** The semigroup algebra $K[q]/I_G$ is normal if and only if $K[q]/I_G$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $G$ is free of $K_5$ minors. This conjecture relates algebraic properties of cut ideals to the minor structure of the underlying graph; its resolution status is not determined by the supplied source information.
object.source_name: Uwe Nagel and Sonja Petrović, “Properties of cut ideals associated to ring graphs”, arXiv:0806.0585 (2009).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.0585

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

object.title: The single-letter characterization of words with trivial fixed-point excess
object.statement:
Let $\mathbf{F}_k$ be the free group on generators $g_1,\ldots,g_k$, let $X_w^{(n)}$ be the number of fixed points of the word map associated with $w$, and let $\sim$ denote the equivalence relation on words used in the paper. **Single-letter characterization conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{E}(X_w^{(n)})\equiv1
$$

if and only if $w$ is equivalent under $\sim$ to a single-letter word.

The conjecture identifies precisely the words for which $\phi(w)=\infty$. It is presented as being suggested by simulations; the source gives no general proof or resolution.
object.source_name: Nati Linial and Doron Puder, “Words Maps and Spectra of Random Graph Lifts”, arXiv:0806.1993 (2009).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.1993

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

object.title: The three-dimensional poset poly-antimatroid staircase conjecture
object.statement:
A **three-dimensional poly-antimatroid** is a poly-antimatroid whose points lie in three dimensions, and a **poset poly-antimatroid** is one closed under intersection. A **step staircase** is the staircase class defined earlier in the paper.

**Three-dimensional staircase conjecture.** Every three-dimensional poset poly-antimatroid is a step staircase.

If true, the result would characterize the three-dimensional poset poly-antimatroids under consideration and, together with the preceding corollary, imply that their convex dimension is at most $3$. The source provides no resolution of this conjecture.
object.source_name: Yulia Kempner and Vadim E. Levit, “Geometry of antimatroidal point sets”, arXiv:0806.2096 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2096

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

object.title: The fundamental-elements conjecture for universal partial fields
object.statement:
Let $N$ be a matroid and let ${\mathbb{P}}_N$ denote its universal partial field. A ${\mathbb{P}}_N$-representation of $N$ is a representation over ${\mathbb{P}}_N$, and two such representations are equivalent in the usual sense. **Fundamental-elements conjecture.** If ${\mathbb{P}}_N$ has finitely many fundamental elements, then all ${\mathbb{P}}_N$-representations of $N$ are equivalent.

The conjecture links the finiteness of the fundamental elements of a universal partial field with uniqueness of the corresponding matroid representations. Its status is not resolved in the source.
object.source_name: R. A. Pendavingh and S. H. M. van Zwam, “Confinement of matroid representations to subsets of partial fields”, arXiv:0806.4487 (2010).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.4487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

object.title: Consecutive-block conjecture for high-multiplicity sumsets
object.statement:
Let $k,l\geqslant 1$ and $n\geqslant 3$ be integers, and write

$$
\kappa:=\left\lfloor\frac{l-1}{n-2}\right\rfloor.
$$

Suppose that $A\subseteq[0,l]$ is an integer set with $0,l\in A$, $\gcd(A)=1$, and $|A|=n$. **Consecutive-block conjecture.** If $k\geqslant 2\kappa+1$, then $kA$ contains a block of consecutive integers of length

$$
(k-\kappa)l+k\bigl((\kappa+1)(n-2)+2-l\bigr).
$$

This conjecture concerns the length of guaranteed consecutive blocks in high-multiplicity sumsets. It is established in the cited work for $k\geqslant 3\kappa$, while the range $2\kappa+1\leqslant k<3\kappa$ remains open to the authors' knowledge.
object.source_name: Vsevolod F. Lev, “Consecutive integers in high-multiplicity sumsets”, arXiv:0806.4580 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.4580

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2008).

object.title: Canonical embedding isomorphism conjecture for spherical latin bitrades
object.statement:
Let $(W,B)$ be a **spherical latin bitrade**, and let $\mathcal{A}_W^*$ and $\mathcal{A}_B^*$ denote the canonical abelian groups into which the white and black trades embed, respectively; write $\mathcal{A}_W$ and $\mathcal{A}_B$ for the corresponding groups without the distinguished embedding data. **Canonical embedding isomorphism conjecture.** If $(W,B)$ is a spherical latin bitrade, then

$$
\mathcal{A}_W^*\cong\mathcal{A}_B^* \quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal{A}_W\cong\mathcal{A}_B.
$$

Although the minimal embeddings of the two trades can differ in general, the conjecture asserts that their canonical embeddings, and the associated abelian groups, coincide up to isomorphism for spherical latin bitrades.
object.source_name: Nicholas J. Cavenagh and Ian M. Wanless, “Latin trades in groups defined on planar triangulations”, arXiv:0807.2707 (2009).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.2707

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2008).

object.title: The Ahlswede–Khachatrian conjecture for cross-t-intersecting families
object.statement:
Let $C(n,k,l,t)$ and $N(n,k,l,t)$ be as above. For integers $i,j$ with $0\le i+j\le n-t$, define

$$
\mathcal G_{ij}(n,k,t)=\left\{F\in\binom{[n]}{k}:|F\cap[t+i+j]|\ge t+i\right\}.
$$

**The cross-intersecting Ahlswede–Khachatrian conjecture.** One has

$$
N(n,k,l,t)=\max_{0\le i+j\le n-t}|\mathcal G_{ij}(n,k,t)|\,|\mathcal G_{ji}(n,l,t)|.
$$

Moreover, up to a permutation of $[n]$, an optimal cross-$t$-intersecting pair is $(\mathcal G_{ij}(n,k,t),\mathcal G_{ji}(n,l,t))$ for some $i,j$. This generalizes the Ahlswede–Khachatrian theorem for ordinary $t$-intersecting families; the corresponding cross-family classification is presented as open.
object.source_name: James Hirschorn, “Asymptotic upper bounds on the shades of t-intersecting families”, arXiv:0808.1434 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1434

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).

object.title: The extremal-shade conjecture for cross-t-intersecting families
object.statement:
Let $C(n,k,l,t)$ be the collection of cross-$t$-intersecting pairs $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$, and define

$$
N_0(n,m_k,m_l,k,l,t)=\max_{(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\in C(n,k,l,t)}|\nabla_{m_k}(\mathcal A)|\,|\nabla_{m_l}(\mathcal B)|.
$$

For $0\le i+j\le n-t$, define $\mathcal G_{ij}(n,k,t)=\{F\in\binom{[n]}{k}:|F\cap[t+i+j]|\ge t+i\}$. **The cross-shade extremal-family conjecture.** One has

$$
N_0(n,m_k,m_l,k,l,t)=\max_{\substack{0\le i\le k-t\\0\le j\le l-t\\i+j\le n-t}}|\mathcal G_{ij}(n,m_k,t)|\,|\mathcal G_{ji}(n,m_l,t)|.
$$

The conjecture is the shade analogue of the proposed extremal description for cross-$t$-intersecting families. The paper gives the definitions and corresponding shade lemma but does not report a resolution.
object.source_name: James Hirschorn, “Asymptotic upper bounds on the shades of t-intersecting families”, arXiv:0808.1434 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1434

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).

object.title: The determinant-character conjecture for finite abelian groups
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$ be two $k$-subsets of $G$. Let $K$ be any field containing an element of multiplicative order $|G|$, and let $\widehat{G}$ be the character group of all group homomorphisms from $G$ to $K^*=K\setminus\{0\}$. **The determinant-character conjecture.** There are $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_k\in\widehat{G}$ such that

$$
\det(\chi_i(a_j))_{1\le i,j\le k}\ne0
$$

and

$$
\det(\chi_i(b_j))_{1\le i,j\le k}\ne0.
$$
 The conjecture is proposed as an exterior-algebra and character formulation whose validity would imply Snevily's conjecture for abelian groups of odd order; the source provides no resolution of it.
object.source_name: Tao Feng, Zhi-Wei Sun and Qing Xiang, “Exterior algebras and two conjectures on finite abelian groups”, arXiv:0808.2753 (2011).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2753

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).

object.title: The power-of-two factor degree conjecture for spanning-tree transfer matrices
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $k$ vertices, let $G_n=G\times P_n$, and let $M$ be the integer $B_k\times B_k$ matrix from the theorem such that $T_n=M^nv[1]$, where $T_n$ is the number of spanning trees in $G_n$. **Power-of-two factor degree conjecture.** The characteristic polynomial $\chi_\lambda(M)$ factors over the integers into monomials whose degree is always a power of $2$. This conjecture concerns the algebraic structure of the transfer matrix governing spanning trees in graph products with paths; the source provides no evidence of resolution.
object.source_name: Paul Raff, “Spanning Trees in Grid Graphs”, arXiv:0809.2551 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.2551

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

object.title: The Coven–Meyerowitz tiling criterion for finite subsets of the integers
object.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}$ be finite, let

$$
A(x)=\sum_{a\in A}x^a,
$$

and let $\Phi_s(x)$ be the $s$-th cyclotomic polynomial, defined by

$$
x^n-1=\prod_{s\mid n}\Phi_s(x).
$$

Define $S_A$ to be the set of prime powers $p^\alpha$ such that $\Phi_{p^\alpha}(x)$ divides $A(x)$.

**Coven–Meyerowitz conjecture.** The set $A$ tiles $\mathbb{Z}$ by translations if and only if:

1. $A(1)=\prod_{s\in S_A}\Phi_s(1)$;
2. whenever $s_1,\ldots,s_k\in S_A$ are powers of different primes, $\Phi_{s_1\cdots s_k}(x)$ divides $A(x)$.

The criterion gives an algebraic characterization of translational tiles through cyclotomic divisibility. The supplied text gives no resolution status for the stated if-and-only-if claim.
object.source_name: Dorim Ervin Dutkay and Palle E. T. Jorgensen, “Duality questions for operators, spectrum and measures”, arXiv:0809.3274 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.3274

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

object.title: The B-factorizability conjecture for complete graphs
object.statement:
Let $V$ be a set of teams, let $PM(V)$ denote the monoid of vectors encoding perfect matchings and HAP data, and let $\overline{\mathbf N}(PM(V))$ be its saturation. A regular graph $G=(V,E)$ is **B-factorizable** if every $v\in\overline{\mathbf N}(PM(V))$ with $v|_K=\chi_E$ already belongs to $\mathbf N(PM(V))$.

**Complete-graph B-factorizability conjecture.** The complete graph $K_{|V|}$ is B-factorizable.

The paper states this as equivalent to Briskorn's conjecture, with the equivalence proved later in the source. Its resolution is not given here.
object.source_name: Kenji Kashiwabara, “Sports scheduling for not all pairs of teams”, arXiv:0809.3682 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.3682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

object.title: The complete-bipartite B-factorizability conjecture
object.statement:
For a regular graph $G=(V,E)$, call $G$ **B-factorizable** if every saturated monoid element with edge component equal to the graph's characteristic vector belongs to the monoid generated by compatible perfect matchings.

**Complete-bipartite B-factorizability conjecture.** Every complete bipartite graph $K_{k,k}$ is B-factorizable.

The source proves the case $K_{4,4}$ and notes that the cases with more vertices were unresolved there.
object.source_name: Kenji Kashiwabara, “Sports scheduling for not all pairs of teams”, arXiv:0809.3682 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.3682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

object.title: Type A restriction is weakly multiplicity-free
object.statement:
Let ${\mathscr{H}}$ be the Hecke algebra of $(W,S)=({\mathcal{S}}_n,\{s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}\})$, and let $J\subseteq S$ satisfy

$$
|J|=|S|-1.
$$

A restriction is **weakly multiplicity-free** when there is at most one cell with each possible local sequence. **Type A restriction conjecture.** The restriction $({\mathscr{H}}_J\otimes_J{\mathscr{H}},{\mathscr{H}})$ is weakly multiplicity-free.

This asks whether restriction from the type $A_{n-1}$ Hecke algebra to a maximal parabolic subalgebra has the weak multiplicity-free property. The corresponding assertion fails for types $B_2$ and $B_3$ in the equal-parameter setting, while the type $A$ case is proposed here and remains open in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Jonah Blasiak, “W-graph versions of tensoring with the §_n defining representation”, arXiv:0809.4810 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.4810

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

object.title: The equality of the sharp and recursive Potts constants
object.statement:
Let $q$ be the number of Potts symbols, let $H$ and $R g$ be the functions defined from the Potts recursion, and define

$$
\hat c(\beta,q):=\sup_{p\in P,\,p_2=\dots=p_q}\frac{H(p_1,\dots,p_q)}{R g(p_1,\dots,p_q)}.
$$

Here $\bar c(\beta,q)$ is the constant appearing in the paper's linear recursion bound.

**Equality conjecture.** We believe that

$$
\hat c(\beta,q)=\bar c(\beta,q).
$$

This conjecture concerns whether the variational constant obtained by restricting to vectors with equal coordinates $p_2=\dots=p_q$ coincides with the constant used in the reconstruction estimate. The source gives no resolution of this claim.
object.source_name: M. Formentin and C. Kuelske, “On the Purity of the free boundary condition Potts measure on random trees”, arXiv:0810.0677 (2009).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.0677

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2008).

object.title: Gal's arithmetic positivity conjecture for Kerov polynomials
object.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\Sigma_{p+1}$ be the Kerov character polynomial on a cycle of length $p+1$, with $R_i$ denoting the free cumulants. **Gal's conjecture.** The expression

$$
\frac{\Sigma_{p+1}-R_{p+2}+R_3}{p}
$$

is a polynomial in $R_2,R_3,\dots$ with non-negative integer coefficients.

The conjecture was formulated by Światosław Gal from numerical calculations and extends the arithmetic positivity results proved in the preceding proposition for related prime-indexed expressions. The source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Maciej Dołega, Valentin Féray and Piotr Sniady, “Explicit combinatorial interpretation of Kerov character polynomials as numbers of permutation factorizations”, arXiv:0810.3209 (2011).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.3209

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2008).

object.title: Conjecture on the affine full-dimensionality of D-optimal factorial designs
object.statement:
Let $r$ denote the number of runs, and distinguish **affinely full-dimensional factorial designs** from **subset fractional factorial designs**. **The D-optimal design conjecture.** The $D$-optimal design is affinely full-dimensional factorial when

$$
r\equiv 5,6,7\pmod{8},
$$

and it is subset fractional factorial when

$$
r\equiv 0,1,2,3,4\pmod{8}.
$$

The conjecture records the periodicity observed in the table of known maximal determinants and predicts the type of $D$-optimal design according to $r$ modulo $8$. The source gives no resolution or status evidence.
object.source_name: Satoshi Aoki and Akimichi Takemura, “Some characterizations of affinely full-dimensional factorial designs”, arXiv:0812.0196 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.0196

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

object.title: Terai's conjecture on h-vectors of Buchsbaum complexes
object.statement: A vector $h=(1,h_1,\dots,h_d) \in \mathbb{Z}^{d+1}$ is the $h$-vector of a $(d-1)$-dimensional Buchsbaum complex $\Delta$ such that $\beta_k(\Delta)=0$ for $k \leq d-3$. A vector $(1,h_1,\dots,h_d) \in \mathbb{Z}^{d+1}$ is an **$M$-vector** if $h_1 \geq 0$ and $0 \leq h_{i+1} \leq h_i^{\langle i \rangle}$ for $i=1,2,\dots,d-1$. **Terai's conjecture.** The vector $h$ has the stated property if and only if: (a) $(1,h_1,\dots,h_{d-1})$ is an $M$-vector; and (b) $-\frac{1}{d}h_{d-1} \leq h_d \leq h_{d-1}^{\langle d-1\rangle}$. This conjecture gives numerical conditions characterizing the $h$-vectors of Buchsbaum complexes with the specified vanishing Betti numbers; the paper proves the relevant two-dimensional cases, while the general statement is the conjectural assertion.
object.source_name: Satoshi Murai, “Face vectors of two-dimensional Buchsbaum complexes”, arXiv:0812.0215 (2009).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.0215

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

object.title: Vanishing matching-sum conjecture for odd square-grid cylinders
object.statement:
Let $C_{m,n}$ be the square-grid cylinder, let $Q_2$ be the class of configurations specified in the surrounding construction, and let $\pi$ be the associated projection map. For $\sigma\in Q_2$, consider all $\tau$ with $\pi(\tau)=\pi(\sigma)$. **Vanishing matching-sum conjecture.** If $n$ is odd, then

$$
\sum_{\tau:\,\pi(\tau)=\pi(\sigma)}(-1)^{|\tau|}=0.
$$

The supplied context gives no resolution and does not fully define $Q_2$ or $\pi$.
object.source_name: Johan Thapper, “Independence Complexes of Cylinders Constructed from Square and Hexagonal Grid Graphs”, arXiv:0812.1165 (2008).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.1165

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2008). “These conjectures were proven in [Jonsson, Electronic J. Combin., 13(1) (2006), R67].”

object.title: The consistency and self-duality conjecture for weighted-game chains
object.statement: Let $J_n$ be the poset of linear games on $n$ voters, let $\mathcal{W}_n$ be its weighted-games subposet, and let $\mathcal{C}_n$ denote the weighted voting polygon. A saturated chain is **consistent** when the ordering it induces on shift-minimal winning coalitions reduces to a consistent set of inequalities; it is **self-dual** when it is invariant under the relevant duality operation. **Consistency and self-duality conjecture.** Every maximal saturated chain that is both consistent and self-dual is associated to some vertical line segment in $\mathcal{C}_n$ lying above a generic weight vector. The conjecture proposes that consistency and self-duality, which are stated as necessary conditions, are also sufficient; the paper does not establish this.
object.source_name: Sarah Mason and Jason Parsley, “A geometric and combinatorial view of weighted voting”, arXiv:1109.1082 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.1082

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2011).
